review_mode: manual evidence review; source-grounded examples, NOT generated playlists or blinded listening test
selection_bias: Cases and positive/negative labels are curated by researchers, not randomly drawn. No statistical quality estimate.

henry.work: Variations pour une porte et un soupir

documented: driving rhythm section and epic crescendos
long freestyle over an existing beat
turntable slowing and phrase repetition documented by UH

ono.work: Voice Piece for Soprano (1961 instruction work)
documented: not inherently a fixed commercially released song recording

cases.mechanism: Reworking recorded material into composed structure across fixed-media composition and experimental rock
cases.baseline: Genre and era axes separate electroacoustic composition from 1970s post-punk/rock; generic tape vocabulary is present, but no explicit distinction between sound source and compositional operation.
cases.shadow: Connect at the level of fixed-media transformation, noting Pierre Henry's door/breath materials versus This Heat's rhythmic looping.
cases.limitations: Looping drums and transforming non-pitched object sounds have different listening dynamics. No provider-level exact-match check or human hearing comparison.

cases.mechanism: Ensemble vocal response and staged intensification despite unrelated musical traditions
cases.baseline: Qawwali and zeuhl/experimental-rock live in different scene categories; repetition alone is too general.
cases.shadow: Bridge via collective vocal intensification and group exchange; retain devotional lyrics and seven-movement rock-suite distinction.
cases.limitations: No claim of direct influence or comparable sacred context. Album-level Magma source, not track-version-level match; requires listening/sequencing review.

cases.mechanism: Recorded rhythmic material actively re-edited to become the composition
cases.baseline: Post-punk tape loops and Southern hip-hop are very distant scene entries; tape manipulation, though already in baseline, has no role-typed bridge.
cases.shadow: Bridge via loop/phrase recomposition and altered perceived rhythmic time; explain cassette/turntable culture and studio editing as distinct workflows.
cases.limitations: June 27th is a long mixtape, not an ordinary track; no evidence of influence or a confirmed Spotify playable recording for either exact version.

cases.mechanism: Recorded environmental/noninstrument sounds entering fixed-media compositions
cases.baseline: Both explicitly electroacoustic and tape-based: existing era and technique vocabulary is enough to consider them.
cases.shadow: Differentiate recognizable object variation (Henry) from documentary field-sound editing (Ferrari), useful for explanation but not novel candidate discovery.
cases.limitations: Composition vs edition/version distinctions need track-level checks.

cases.mechanism: Only the word repetition; Magma is ensemble-driven, This Heat loop/fixed-media-driven
cases.baseline: Repetition plus avant-rock could overgeneralize the pair.
cases.shadow: Reject as a *method* bridge unless a specific verified recording offers stronger shared roles or sonic motion.
cases.limitations: This does not forbid a human choosing both after listening; it rejects the asserted evidence.

cases.mechanism: Both repeat phrases but for fundamentally different social and musical functions
cases.baseline: Both can be described as hypnotic repeated phrases, which is dangerously broad.
cases.shadow: Reject method-equivalence: qawwali's devotional ensemble refrains vs hip-hop DJ's tape/crossfader/pitch intervention.
cases.limitations: Shared words don't create equivalent cultural context; still may share a particular *audible* quality after listening.

cases.mechanism: Both recorded onto tape, but environmental documentation is not necessarily rhythmic looping
cases.baseline: Tape and experimental labels overlap superficially.
cases.shadow: Reject medium-only match without proof of shared manipulation technique or audible rhythm.
cases.limitations: Could be reconsidered if a specific track passage demonstrably uses a stronger joint operation.

cases.mechanism: Both use extended voice, but one is a documented audio poem and the other a performance instruction
cases.baseline: An artist-level tag match might treat both as eligible audio tracks.
cases.shadow: Reject as a direct playlist-ready pair without a specific recording of Ono's instruction performance; medium/type guardrail first.
cases.limitations: MoMA documents an actual performance; a recording may exist, but not automatically a commercially playable canonical track.
